meaning: of Ashworth, a chapelry in the parish of Middleton, co. Lanc., anciently Asseheworth
author_comment: This small place (pop. 233 in 1861) has given birth to a surname that has become largely represented. It is familiar to every town and village in south Lancashire. Henry Ashworth (1794-1880), the friend of Cobden, was born at Birtwistle, near Bolton, a few miles from Ashworth, on Sept. 4, 1794. Caleb Ashworth, D.D. (1722-75), a celebrated dissenter, was born at Rossendale, co. Lanc. John Ashworth (1813-75), preacher, manufacturer, and author, was born at Cutgate, near Rochdale; v. Dict. Nat. Biog. ii. 187-8. The little village has kept itself well in the remembrance of Lancashire people.
notes: Cited in the author's commentary; the friend of Cobden; born at Birtwistle, near Bolton, Sept. 4, 1794
source: Dictionary of National Biography, vol. ii, pp. 187-8
